title: fix: CLI oldpin buffer not zeroed on read_pin failure path
description:
In src/cli/wp11_cli.c ~line 1048-1051, if read_pin() fails (returns < 0), the function prints an error and returns 1 without calling memset(oldpin, 0, sizeof(oldpin)).

The oldpin buffer contains partial or complete plaintext PIN input from the user. Leaving it unzeroed means the PIN persists in process stack memory until overwritten by subsequent function calls — potentially readable via core dump, /proc/PID/mem, or a heap/stack scanner.

All other PIN error paths in the function (line ~1059, 1067, 1072, 1077) correctly zero their PIN buffers before returning.

Fix: Add memset(oldpin, 0, sizeof(oldpin)) before the return at line 1051. Consider using explicit_bzero() or wc_MemZero() instead of memset, which the compiler may optimize away.
